overview: This bill, the CRACKDOWN Act, sets a limit on improper payments in the Child Care and Development Block Grant program, the main federal program that gives states money to help low-income families pay for child care. Improper payments are payments that should not have been made or were made in the wrong amount, whether through fraud or error. If more than 5 percent of a state's payments in a year are improper, the state must submit a plan to the Department of Health and Human Services to bring the rate down and report on its progress. If the rate stays above 5 percent for two years in a row, the state would lose its funding unless it convinces the department that it will get below 5 percent or make significant progress on its plan the next year. As of April 6, 2026, a House committee had approved it and it was placed on the House calendar.
for: Supporters say a clear threshold with real consequences pushes states to fix weak controls and protect federal child care money from waste and fraud.
against: Critics say cutting off a state's funding would hurt low-income families who rely on child care help, punishing them for problems in state administration.
